TimeEstimate.title: Time estimate
TimeEstimate.description: The expected effort for one object in another app: how many hours it is thought to take, optionally per role, and whether that number is a ceiling. The expected number belongs to the consuming app, which writes it from its own policy: a case type's budgeted hours, a project's planned effort. The object, the derived remainder and the enforcement belong to humaniq (estimate-spent-and-remaining-on-an-hours-leaf, REQ-HL-EST-005). Remaining effort is NEVER stored: it is estimated minus booked, computed on read, so deleting an entry moves it at once.

domainObjectType.title: Object type
domainObjectType.description: Which kind of object this estimate is for, as app:schema.
domainObjectType.x-notes: The hours-leaf shape, verbatim: the `<app>:<schema>` literal, for example dossiq:zaak. The app id is the `<id>` in that app's appinfo/info.xml, so this literal moves when an app is renamed and not before.

domainObjectRef.title: Object
domainObjectRef.description: The uuid of the object this estimate is for.
domainObjectRef.x-notes: A plain string rather than a $ref, because the object lives in another app's register. Set together with domainObjectType or not at all.

estimatedHours.title: Estimated hours
estimatedHours.description: How many hours this is expected to take.

role.title: Role
role.description: Which role these hours are expected from. Leave empty for the object as a whole.
role.x-notes: Matched against TimeEntry.role. An object may carry one estimate per role plus at most one estimate with no role; a second estimate for the same object and the same role is refused by TimeEstimateListener (REQ-HL-EST-001), because two expected numbers for one role give two remainders and nothing looks wrong.

enforced.title: Hard ceiling
enforced.description: Whether a booking that would pass this number is refused.
enforced.x-notes: REQ-HL-EST-004. False by default and refuses nothing: an estimate is a plan, and most plans are not budgets. When true, a NEW entry past the ceiling is refused in the write path naming the estimate, the ceiling and the hours left, while STOPPING A RUNNING TIMER always lands, because time already worked is a fact and a register that refuses a fact reports a smaller number than the truth.

note.title: Note
note.description: Where this number comes from, in one line.

TimeEntry.x-notes: estimate-spent-and-remaining-on-an-hours-leaf: the booking gains the role it was worked in, so an estimate per role has something to count against. It is the ONLY field this change adds to TimeEntry: spent stays the sum of the entries and remaining is never stored anywhere.

role.title: Role
role.description: Which role these hours were worked in. Leave empty when the object is not split by role.
role.x-notes: Matched against TimeEstimate.role when the remainder is derived and when an enforced ceiling is applied (REQ-HL-EST-001/-004). A free string rather than an enum: a gemeente's roles are its own, and an enum here would make adding one a humaniq release.
